utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have looked at it, and I think that this is now the summary regarding the value of military immovables and their values of the former JNA regarding Serbia and Montenegro and the other republics that have seceded as at 31st of December, 1990, and this reflects the value, expressed in US dollars, of the property that the army had at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I seek its admission under the same terms and conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number and be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D390, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, His Honour had asked you a question earlier, which I'm going to ask you again, which is: With regard to this series of documents that we've looked at in terms of both movable and immovable assets, are these assets that were left by the JNA for the benefit of the ABiH, for the benefit of the VRS, for the benefit of some other institution or institutions, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're asking specifically about Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And the focus -- the focus that His Honour has put on the question, which is specifically Bosnia-Herzegovina. Obviously, that would define the ABiH and the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I believe that we are talking here about two different issues. One issue is the stock-taking of the JNA assets on the 31st of December, 1990, and the second issue is that we have summaries of what was left in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, you can take this particular document off the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to your last answer and specifically with regard to the second issue of summaries of what was left in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, are those summaries of what was left in the territory of the Bosnia-Herzegovina left for the ABiH, for the VRS, if you know, or for some other institution or organisation?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: If I have seen the summary in detail, we are talking about the entire bulk of assets that the JNA had in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, how this was divided at a later stage is a completely different issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to what you've just said, to your knowledge was there agreement to leave military assets, when the JNA left, for the benefit of the ABiH Army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I don't think I can give you a precise answer to that. However, I don't think there was any agreement reached though.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to go to the issue of the special-purpose industry, if I might. Before the break-up of the former Yugoslavia, could you estimate for us, if you know, the extent to which the economy was based on the military industry or military production and manufacture?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I can't give you an estimation. I know that at least 50 per cent remained in the aforementioned republics, and 50 per cent remain in the FRY. Now, what was the contribution of those to the economy as a whole? I can't give you even a rough answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm asking you a slightly different question. Before the break-up of the former Yugoslavia, there are those that have said that the majority of the industry was predicated upon the production of military goods and that the former Yugoslavia was a nation that was increasingly becoming a nation that was producing military goods for both internal use as well as for export to other nations, formally, before the break-up.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: All I know is that the special-purpose industry or the military complex manufactured up to 80 per cent of weapons and equipment for the army, which means that the army received these domestically-manufactured products. There were years in which the value of our exports of weapon and equipment amounted even up to two billion US dollars. However, what was the proportion of that amount with regard to the total state revenue, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could you tell us, During the period of time that it was receiving an annual revenue up of to some two billion dollars, as you've estimated it, if you know, where was the former Yugoslavia in terms of production of what I call military goods? Could you -- could you give it a ranking? Was it 1st, 2nd, 5th, 7th, 12th?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: You know, I'm an engineer, and I can only speak from that point of view, by applying certain criteria. I have heard and there were reports in the press that we were the fourth or the fifth or the sixth exporting country. However, which criteria were used in order to achieve -- or, rather, to come to this conclusion, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood. With regard to the issue of special-purpose industry, prior to the break-up, could you tell us, if you know, how many locations there were throughout the country of special-purpose industry factories or research departments or locations?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I might, if we could have 3370D up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In a moment. All right. Taking a look at this particular map, I note on this map that there are a number of areas that designate a special -- there are a number of areas on the map that have numbers upon them. Can you identify for us what those numbers represent?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Sir, this represents where the technical services were located but not for special purposes. This was part of the army; they were subordinated to the army. Whereas special-purposes production was, so to speak, was subordinated to the Ministry of Defence or worked under their auspices, so to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let's stay with this map then. We'll discuss this matter, and then we'll tie that into the special-purpose industry in a moment. Could you tell us, considering your answer, what number 1 on the map stands for?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Number 1 is the repair and maintenance institute in Cacak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Number 2?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Number 2 is the technical -- the repair and maintenance institute for ammunition based in Kragujevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And number 3?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: This is the air force repair institute, Batajnica, in Belgrade, and they were responsible for air force equipment and for their logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Number 4.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: This is the navy repair institute, Tivat, in Montenegro, and they would repair and maintain navy equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Regards to 1, 2, and 3, those all seem to be designated in the geographical location of Serbia. Were those specific institutes under your technical administration?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: 1 and 2 are under my administration, the repairs institute in Cacak and Kragujevac. Number 3, the Batajnica repairer's institute, was under the chief of the air force administration within the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I understood your testimony earlier, the reason that number 3 would not be under your authority was because it was air force and not land army and you were responsible for land army issues.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if my friend could particularise that -- those two questions as to time. As we know, there's be a re-organisation of the MOD in the General Staff that occurred at a period near the beginning of our indictment, and I just want to place the answers in the appropriate time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'd be happy to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to Cacak and Kragujevac, when you were the chief -- when they were under your technical administration, what years are we referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: At the time of the JNA and at the time of the SRJ -- or, rather, the FRY, F-R-Y.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to give years? From what year to what year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from the time that I was appointed as chief and then up until the time I was transferred to the Ministry of Defence. All these institutions are still under those logistics sectors in the army to this very day, 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you remind us when you were appointed the chief and when you were transferred to the Ministry of Defence? I know you've mentioned this earlier, but if you could just remind us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1993 until 1999 I was the chief of the technical administration, and in the year 2000 towards the end of March and the beginning of April, on the 2nd of April, I was transferred to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to number 4, I heard the word "navy," so was -- I immediately questioned whether or not that was a technical area that was under your -- that was under your authority, because you said "navy." Was it? The area that was in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: No. That was under the navy technical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to numbers -- well, number 5. That's in the geographic location of Croatia according to this map. First of all, which institute was that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That was the air force repairs institute in Velika Gorica. They repaired and maintained aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In 1993, was that particular repairs institute a repairs institute that did work for or in conjunction with the VJ, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Up until 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: No. It was no longer part of the Army of Yugoslavia then.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you -- do you know when it ceased being part of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: No, I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You previously had indicated that Croatia was one of the republics that had seceded from the former entire -- the SFRY, let me put it that way. And when Croatia seceded from the SFRY, was it at or about that time or that specific date that this particular institute ceased being an institute that was under the auspices of the army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: During that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that army was -- that army was the JNA or the VJ, just so we're clear, because I know that you've used both JNA and VJ, depending on whether we're talking about before or after the break-up.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: It was the JNA at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. With regard to number 6 on the map, what was that institute?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That's the repairs and maintenance institute Bregana. It says it's in Croatia here, but the institute itself was, in fact, in Croatia, but all the employees -- or most of the employees, at least, were located in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And it was a repair and maintenance institute for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That institute was under the authority of the technical administration. It would repair and maintain non-combat vehicles, artillery pieces, and some of the artillery. Artillery, ammunition, and some artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After Slovenia and Croatia engaged in their secession, was that particular institute part of the support of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: No. It was immediately put in their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "put in their hands," whose hands?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The hands of the Army of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to number 7, could you identify that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Number 7 is the navy repairs institute located in Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to this particular institute located in Sibenik, was that again something that became a Croatian institute for the benefit of the Croatian military after Croatia seceded, as you put it?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Number 8?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The navy repairs institute in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I -- would it be fair to say that your answer would be the same with regard to number 8 as it was with regard to those other institutes that are located in the geographic area of Croatia and -- and Slovenia, as you mentioned, with regard to what is designated as number 6 on this particular map?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Number 9, please.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: This is the air force repairs institute in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And under whose auspices was the air force supplies institute in Banja Luka after the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, we didn't have a repairs institute in Banja Luka. I don't know where this information was obtained, but I know -- not familiar with any such case. Perhaps Kosmos, the factory, is what they had in mind, but I'm not aware of the fact that there was a repairs institute located in Banja Luka. We're obviously dealing with an air force repairs institute here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Was -- was that an air force repairs institute that was under the auspices of the VJ or under the auspices of another army, if you know?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you that I'm not aware of the existence of a repairs institute there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. With regard to number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The Rajlovac air force repairs institute. As far as I know, it fell into the hands of Republika Srpska. It's on the border of the territory there, so I can't say for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say that the territory of the Republic of Srpska, did the Republic of Srpska have its own army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And what army was that? What was the name of that army?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Looking at number 11, if we could. Could you identify that for us?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: It's not correctly written here. It's the technical repairs institute - not the VRZ, not the air force repairs institute - in Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you say it's a technical repairs institute, and what is the distinction between --

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: What is the distinction between a technical institute and what is written here?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: A technical repairs institute -- well, a technical department called all its services technical repair institutes. But in the case of the air force, it was called the air force repairs institute; in the case of the navy, the navy repairs institute. These are the relevant abbreviations that are used. And this institute was under the technical administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say it "was under the technical administration," once again the same question that I've asked before: After a point in time, and you've introduced a -- the Republika Srpska into your discussion, was this particular technical repairs institute part of the Republika Srpska, part of the ABiH, Bosnia-Herzegovina, a part of FRY?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: After the events, it was the repairs institute -- or a repairs institute of the ABiH, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did it remain that, or did it at some point in time become a repair institute for any other country, as you recall?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I think that this repairs institute was subsequently destroyed. It no longer existed. It was no longer involved in that sphere of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. And, finally, number 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But just before we go to number 12. Before it was destroyed, did it belong to any other country other than Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm going back to your question, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So I assume that the letters that are written in brackets on the legend on this map denote the country to which these belong. Now, I see there is "RS" in brackets after number 11. Is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And, finally, number 12 on this particular map. Could you identify that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the technical repairs institute in Travnik. It was involved in repairing and maintaining electronics for weapon systems. It was part of the technical administration, while this was still possible. Subsequently, it became part of the ABiH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you say "subsequently became part of the ABiH army," you have used the term on a number of occasions of "after the events." Are we to take that to mean after the various secessions of the republics that you referred to before, when you use the term "after the events"?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I'm using that term deliberately because it was a dynamic process, and some institutes even fell into the hands of Bosnia and Herzegovina or Croatia prior to the establishment of the various republics or the various states.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't. Then when you say "after the events," what events are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the time at which Republika Srpska was declared; the existence of Republika Srpska, as well as the existence of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I seek this document's admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D391, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And we've been -- we've been discussing briefly the issue of technical institutes, and I think we were somewhat waylaid because I started off the discussion with regard to the issue of special-purpose industries. So if you could bear with me. Could you define for us what special-purpose industries are?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I can say a few words about the subject. This was an industry in the SFRY that was adapted to produce weapons and military equipment in accordance with the requests made by the relevant ministries.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when -- was this a single industry, or were these a number of different industries with -- that had different functions?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: This industry was represented by a number of companies in the territory of the SFRY, and the intention was for each republic to have certain possibilities to satisfy the needs of the JNA. And everyone participated in the budget.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I understand we're talking about the SFRY. And do you know what the considerations were with regard to, as you put it, the intention for each republic to have certain possibilities to satisfy the needs of the JNA? Was that -- if you know, was that an economic consideration? Was that a military consideration? Was it a combination of considerations that focused on the intention being for each republic to have certain possibilities to satisfy the needs?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: As an engineer, I can say that the main criterion was that each republic should participate in carrying out certain tasks and should be able to benefit from the military industry. Another criterion was that part of the special-purposes production should be located in the central part of the state, mainly in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so that the industry would be protected in the case of a possible attack. But the main criterion - and I know this for sure because I was at the head of the sector for a year or so - the main criterion was that each republic should participate in producing weapons and military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You've just mentioned something which is that the special-purposes production should be located in the central part of the state, mainly in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so that the industry would be protected in the case of a possibility of attack, and I'm wondering whether or not you can give us any other information about that, because it sounds to me like you're discussing one of the underlying principles that existed in the SFRY with regard to the kind of structure the military had and the kinds of concerns that it had. And if I'm being too vague, part of what -- part of what I'm thinking about is that you had previously mentioned that you were neither a NATO nation nor a Warsaw Pact nation, and that you were -- you haven't said that you were sandwiched in between the two, but, geographically, the SFRY held somewhat of a unique position.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I think that your question contains the answer. We considered the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be the bulwark from which the entire Yugoslavia could be defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And I apologise to Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In terms of the special-purpose industry's ability to do business, were they under the SFRY? Were they allowed to do business domestically, internationally, both, either, neither?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: As far as that is concerned, I can say that there were certain regulations that made this possible, and they could engage in business for the army and on the local market, and they could also export. Much of what was produced for special purposes was intended for export.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And with regard to that which was produced, which was intended for export, if you know, were the nature of those contracts? Were those contracts that existed with the state, or were those contracts that existed with the specific special-purpose industry itself, or both?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: No. On the whole, we had state contracts, contracts with Federal Ministry of Defence. They would draw up the contracts. Institutes that had been authorised by the Ministry of Defence to do this would draft that contracts, the SDPR or the supplies administration within the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Using the term "Ministry of Defence," and I'm of some confusion here, under the SFRY was the Ministry of Defence an independent organ of the state, or was it part and parcel of another organ? Was it a unified system there or was there a distinction?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I was vague. I was talking about the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, abbreviated SSNO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Is the SSNO, just so that we're clear, the SSNO and the Ministry of Defence, are those the same kinds of -- of organs, or are there some distinctions between those two organs, the SSNO and the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The only difference was that the SSNO existed until the break-up of the country, and after that we had the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. After the break-up of the country, did the special-purpose industries have the right to privately contract with foreign entities, whatever they may be?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: That was a difficult period for the special-purpose industry, when the needs for equipment and equipment were reduced due to the lack of funds. Therefore, each factory had to find its own way of coping with the situation. As much as I'm able to reply to your question, I don't think that any of them concluded any contract directly. I think it all had to go through the SDPR. That is to say, while I was at the head of that department, we didn't conclude a single contract -- or, rather, no factory concluded a single contract with anyone without the consent of my administration or at least its approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: You indicated that there was a difficult period for the special-purpose industry when the needs for equipment and equipment were reduced due to lack of funds. When you're referring to the issue of lack of funds, which lack of funds are you referring to? Whose lack of funds are being identified there?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: With regard to the needs of the army, certain funds are earmarked in the budget for procurement of equipment locally. Since the state lacked enough funds for these specific purposes, this caused the shortage of financial means for procuring locally whatever was needed by the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before the break-up of the SFRY, can you tell us, if you know, about how many factories that were distributed throughout the republic, as you've explained to us, existed? Throughout the country, in total, if you can.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I think that there were several dozens. Let's say between 80 or 90 factories within the industry complex. However, this complex expanded by engaging subcontractors for the production process, so that we can say that even thousands of businesses or companies were involved in the protection, of course, with different percentage of participates and different revenues generated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After, when the SFRY broke up and you had the FRY, could you tell us about how many special-purpose industry factories were contained within the -- within FRY?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: After the break-up of the country, approximately 14 factories and enterprises remained in the FRY. And later, this number increased to 14 or 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Now, before the break-up of the FRY, were the special-purpose industries throughout the country independent or interdependent on each other? I'm sorry, let me say that -- independent of each other or interdependent on each other?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was precisely what caused the problem, because they were totally dependent on each other. In most cases, it was impossible for one single factory to produce one final product. It had to be manufactured by at least three or four different companies. For example, if you wanted to produce a rifle bullet, it involved at least the involvement of five companies in the process.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, after the war started, did the special-purpose industries stopped working with each other? Did they continue working with each other? What happened if there was this -- a reality of the interdependence of these companies working with each other in order to finalise a product?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: The majority of equipment and weapons were planned to produce by way of co-operation between the companies from Slovenia via Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia, and in some instances even it included Montenegro and Macedonia. After the break-up, we tried to produce as many elements in our factories in order to supersede the input of the factories that remained in other republics. For that purpose, we provided certain documents to the government through the Ministry of Defence, and that was the so-called process of transfer of production of military equipment from other areas to the territory of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand that. But with regard to the question that I've asked you, did the co-operation between special-purpose industries in various republics, including, for example, the FRY and BiH and Croatia, continue or discontinue after the war started?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Now I understand your question. This co-operation was not discontinued, notwithstanding a very difficult situation which sometimes amounted to war. Even under such difficult circumstances they tried to co-operate as much as they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we're waiting for Mr. Guy-Smith, can you tell us, What does "SDPR" stand for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. It's a federal institution intended for analysing foreign markets and adapting its capacities to it and then to work through its representative offices abroad towards selling military equipment produced in the SFRY and in the Republic of Serbia nowadays, and it stands for Federal Administration or Directorate for Trading in Special-Purpose Products.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the special-purpose industry in FRY, can you tell us whether or not the special-purpose industries in FRY were reliant on either the special-purpose industries in the BiH and/or Croatia for production of such things as tanks, bullets, mines, and other weapons of war?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: I don't know which period you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After the war started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Hold on. His Honour's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you have my question in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUGOSLAV KODZOPELJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard your question. After the outbreak of war, although there were problems in this co-operation, people found a way to deal with that because it was a matter of survival for them and their families as well. So these institutions continued to co-operate to the extent that it was possible. Of course, it was burdened with various problems, but they did continue to work together wherever it was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We, unfortunately, have to break up now. We can't finish with you because the next Court must come in. You will have to come back tomorrow again at 9.00 in the same courtroom. While you are out of court, I may just warn you that you are -- you may not discuss the case with anybody, least of all counsel for the Defence, until you finish your testimony. I see you're nodding. I guess that means you do understand. And, therefore, court adjourned to 9.00 tomorrow morning, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 6th day of July, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
